parts.text: During famine in Judah, Elimelech takes Naomi and their two sons to Moab. He dies, and the sons marry Moabite women, Orpah and Ruth, but they also die. Hearing that the LORD has provided food for his people, Naomi sets out for home. She urges her daughters-in-law to remain and find new husbands, explaining her own helplessness and bitter loss. Orpah returns, but Ruth clings to her.

Ruth pledges to go where Naomi goes, belong to her people, worship her God, and share her burial place. Naomi accepts her resolve. They arrive in Beth-lehem at the beginning of barley harvest. Naomi asks to be called Mara rather than Naomi, describing herself as emptied and afflicted by the Almighty.

Ruth goes to glean for food and comes to a field belonging to Boaz, a relative of Naomi’s late husband. Boaz notices her, learns of her faithful service to Naomi, and gives her protection, water, and permission to remain with his workers. Ruth wonders at his kindness to a stranger. He acknowledges her choice to leave her homeland and seek refuge under the LORD’s wings.

Boaz includes Ruth at the meal and instructs his men to leave extra grain without rebuking her. She returns with a generous harvest and leftover food. Naomi blesses Boaz and identifies him as one of their near kinsmen. She encourages Ruth to stay in his fields for safety, and Ruth continues through barley and wheat harvests while living with Naomi.

chapters.title: Ruth asks Boaz to act as a kinsman

parts.text: Naomi seeks a settled home for Ruth and instructs her to wash, dress, and go discreetly to Boaz’s threshingfloor. After he lies down, Ruth uncovers his feet and lies there. Waking at midnight, Boaz asks who she is. She identifies herself and asks him to spread his skirt over her because he is a near kinsman.

Boaz blesses Ruth for her kindness and praises her reputation as a virtuous woman. He promises to act but explains that another kinsman has a prior claim. Ruth remains until morning and leaves before being recognized. Boaz gives her barley to take to Naomi. Hearing the account, Naomi tells Ruth to wait, confident Boaz will settle the matter that day.

chapters.title: Boaz redeems the inheritance and marries Ruth

parts.text: At the city gate, Boaz assembles the nearer kinsman and ten elders. The man initially agrees to redeem Elimelech’s land, but withdraws when Boaz explains the obligation involving Ruth and preservation of the dead man’s name. He gives Boaz his right, confirmed by the customary removal of a shoe. Boaz publicly acquires the property and takes Ruth as wife, and the witnesses pronounce blessings.

The LORD gives Ruth a son. Beth-lehem’s women praise God for providing Naomi with continuing family care and comfort through the child and the daughter-in-law who loves her. Naomi cares for the boy, named Obed, who becomes Jesse’s father and David’s grandfather. The closing genealogy traces the family from Pharez through Boaz and Obed to David.
